title: Exponential regression
intro: Fit positive paired data and tell interpolation from extrapolation.

beats.spoken: Each row records dough volume at one hour. Every volume must be positive because exponential regression fits the natural log of y.
beats.coach: Lists xval and yval are already named. Time is x and dough volume is y. ExpReg fits ln(y), so every y must be positive.

beats.spoken: Open Statistics, then Stat Calculations. Press the letter A, even if the option is below the visible list.
beats.coach: Menu → 4 Statistics → 1 Stat Calculations → A Exponential Regression. A selects it even if it is below the visible menu.

beats.spoken: Use the right arrow and Tab. Set the list called x val as the X List and y val as the Y List.
beats.coach: From X List: Right to open; Tab confirms xval and moves to Y. Right to open Y, Right again to select yval, then Tab.

beats.spoken: Use each pair once. Save to f one and keep the results in C and D. Press Enter.
beats.coach: Check Frequency List 1, fit stored to f1 and results starting in C. Press Enter to calculate.

beats.spoken: Read a and b. The value a is the estimate at x equals zero. It need not equal the measurement there.
beats.coach: In ŷ = a·bˣ, a ≈ 24.294 is the model at x = 0. It need not equal the actual reading of 24.

beats.spoken: A one-unit rise in x multiplies the estimate by b. Here that is about a fifty point seven percent increase.
beats.coach: b ≈ 1.50682 is a multiplier: an extra hour adds about 50.7% to the prediction, not 50.7 units.

beats.spoken: The r and r squared rows assess the line fitted to x and the natural log of y, not the raw readings.
beats.coach: r and r² describe the fit on the log scale (x, ln(y)), not the raw readings.

beats.spoken: At x equals two point five the input is inside the observed span. Substituting gives an interpolation.
beats.coach: x = 2.5 lies inside [0, 4]: interpolate with the unrounded fitted coefficients to obtain ŷ ≈ 67.7.

beats.spoken: At x equals six the input is outside the observed span. The model can predict, but the trend may not continue.
beats.coach: x = 6 lies outside [0, 4]: extrapolation gives ŷ ≈ 284.4, but the observed trend may not continue.
